title: Mathematics Practice Test 2 - Mathematics - Algebraic Factoring
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Given the function $f(x) = 4x^2 - 14x + 12$, which of the following expressions is equivalent to $f(x)$?
questions.explain: To find the equivalent expression, factor the given quadratic $4x^2 - 14x + 12$. You can first factor out a 2: $2(2x^2 - 7x + 6)$. The quadratic in the parentheses factors to $(2x - 3)(x - 2)$. Thus, the full expression is $2(2x - 3)(x - 2)$. Distributing the 2 into $(x - 2)$ yields $(2x - 3)(2x - 4)$. Alternatively, expanding option 'b' with FOIL gives $(2x)(2x) + (2x)(-3) + (-4)(2x) + (-4)(-3) = 4x^2 - 6x - 8x + 12 = 4x^2 - 14x + 12$.
